'''Masour Ousmane Dembélé'''{{efn-ua|{{IPA|fr|usman dɛmbele}}<ref>{{cite web |title=L'interview « Petit frère » avec Ousmane Dembélé |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yarV_-GbcJw&t=18s |website=YouTube | date=12 September 2025 |publisher=Onze Mondial |access-date=15 November 2025}}</ref>}} (born 15 May 1997) is a French professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] and [[right winger]] for {{French football updater|PSG}} club [[Paris Saint-Germain FC|Paris Saint-Germain]] and the [[France national football team|France national team]]. Regarded as one of the best players in the world,<ref name=":6">{{cite web |date=1 June 2025 |title=Ballon d'Or 2025 Power Rankings: Desire Doue's Champions League final fireworks move PSG teenager into the top 10 – but this is Ousmane Dembele's Golden Ball |last=Maston |first=Tom |url=https://www.goal.com/en/lists/ballon-dor-2025-power-rankings/bltd009fae5576d751f |access-date=3 June 2025 |website=Goal.com |archive-date=14 July 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250714161847/https://www.goal.com/en/lists/ballon-dor-2025-power-rankings/bltd009fae5576d751f |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=":7">{{cite web |last1=Swan |first1=Rob |last2=Malyan |first2=Christy |last3=Murray |first3=Will |date=10 November 2023 |title=The 25 best footballers in the world right now – ranked in order |url=https://www.givemesport.com/best-football-players-in-the-world/ |access-date=3 June 2025 |website=GiveMeSport |archive-date=18 April 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260418121038/https://www.givemesport.com/best-football-players-in-the-world/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=":8">{{cite web |date=14 March 2025 |last=O'Hanlon |first=Ryan |title=After PSG beat Liverpool, we ask: Is Dembélé the world's best soccer player? |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/insider/story/_/id/44237996/ousmane-dembele-psg-liverpool-france-best-player-world |access-date=3 June 2025 |website=ESPN |archive-date=3 June 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250603100718/https://www.espn.com/soccer/insider/story/_/id/44237996/ousmane-dembele-psg-liverpool-france-best-player-world |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Ross-Murray |first=Ewan |title=The 15 Best Players Who Will Be At the 2026 World Cup—Ranked |url=https://www.si.com/soccer/best-players-2026-world-cup-ranked |website=Sports Illustrated |date=March 30, 2026 |access-date=April 28, 2026 |archive-date=29 April 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260429124834/https://www.si.com/soccer/best-players-2026-world-cup-ranked |url-status=live }}</ref> he is one of eleven players to have won the [[FIFA World Cup]], [[UEFA Champions League]], and [[Ballon d'Or]] during their career.

Dembélé began his professional career at [[Stade Rennais FC|Rennes]], where he was named [[Ligue 1 Young Player of the Year]] in his one season with the first team. In 2016, he transferred to the German club [[Borussia Dortmund]], winning the [[DFB-Pokal]] in his debut season and scoring in the [[2017 DFB-Pokal final|final]]. Regarded as one of the most promising young talents in world football, he joined the Spanish club [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] in 2017 for an initial fee of €105 million, making him at the time the [[List of most expensive association football transfers|joint-second most expensive]] player in history, alongside [[Paul Pogba]] and behind [[Neymar]]. Although Dembélé did not fully meet the expectations placed on him at Barcelona, he won multiple domestic honours with the club, including three [[La Liga]] titles, two [[Copa del Rey]] titles, and two [[Supercopa de España]] titles.

Dembélé returned to France in 2023, signing with Paris Saint-Germain for a fee of €50.4 million. In the [[2024–25 Paris Saint-Germain FC season|2024–25 season]], he experienced a resurgence in his career, contributing 33 goals and 15 assists in 49 appearances as PSG won a [[continental treble]]. He was named the [[Ligue 1 Player of the Year]] and the 2025 [[UEFA Champions League#Player of the Season|UEFA Champions League Player of the Season]], as well as finishing as the [[List of Ligue 1 top scorers|Ligue 1 top scorer]]. His performances earned him the [[2025 Ballon d'Or]]. In the [[2025–26 Paris Saint-Germain FC season|following season]], Dembélé was again named the Ligue 1 Player of the Year, and won another [[2025–26 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] and [[2025–26 Ligue 1|league]] title.

After winning 20 caps and scoring five goals at youth level, Dembélé made his senior international debut for France in 2016. He was a member of the France squad that won the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]], also featuring at [[UEFA Euro 2020]], the [[2022 FIFA World Cup|2022 World Cup]] (finishing as [[2022 FIFA World Cup final|runners-up]]), [[UEFA Euro 2024|Euro 2024]], and the [[2026 FIFA World Cup|2026 World Cup]].

==Club career==
===Rennes===
[[File:Saint-Lô - Rennes CFA2 20150523 - Ousmane Dembélé 4.JPG|thumb|upright|left|Dembélé with [[Stade Rennais F.C.|Rennes]] in 2015]]

Dembélé made his senior debut for [[Stade Rennais F.C.|Rennes]]' reserve team in the [[Championnat National 2|Championnat de France Amateur]], on 6 September 2014, coming on as a 78th-minute substitute for [[Zana Allée]]. He effectively set up Alseny Kourouma for the second goal of a 2–0 home win over the reserve team of Breton rivals [[En Avant Guingamp|Guingamp]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Rennes (B) – Guingamp (B) : 2–0 Guingamp n'a pas fait le poids |trans-title=Rennes (B) – Guingamp (B): 2–0 Guingamp were inadequate |url=http://www.letelegramme.fr/autres-sports/rennes-b-guingamp-b-2-0-guingamp-n-a-pas-fait-le-poids-07-09-2014-10328789.php |access-date=13 May 2016 |work=[[Le Télégramme]] |date=7 September 2014 |language=fr |archive-date=2 March 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200302092707/https://www.letelegramme.fr/autres-sports/rennes-b-guingamp-b-2-0-guingamp-n-a-pas-fait-le-poids-07-09-2014-10328789.php |url-status=live }}</ref> On 9 November, he scored his first career goal, again coming off the bench in a game at the Stade de la Piverdière, this time against the reserves of [[Stade Lavallois|Laval]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Rennes en pilotage automatique |trans-title=Rennes on auto-pilot |url=http://www.rennes.maville.com/sport/detail_-rennes-en-pilotage-automatique_52674-2655816_actu.Htm |access-date=13 May 2016 |website=Maville.com |date=10 November 2014 |language=fr |archive-date=2 March 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200302092720/https://rennes.maville.com/sport/detail_-rennes-en-pilotage-automatique_52674-2655816_actu.Htm |url-status=live }}</ref> He totalled 13 goals in 18 games in his first season, including a [[hat-trick]] on 16 May 2015 in a 6–1 win over [[SC Hérouville|Hérouville]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Stade Rennais (B) – Hérouville : 6–1 |url=http://www.ouest-france.fr/bretagne/stade-rennais-b-herouville-6-1-3411620 |access-date=13 May 2016 |work=[[Ouest-France]] |date=17 May 2015 |language=fr |archive-date=2 March 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200302092715/https://www.ouest-france.fr/bretagne/stade-rennais-b-herouville-6-1-3411620 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 6 November 2015, Dembélé made his professional debut for Rennes' first team in [[Ligue 1]] against [[Angers SCO|Angers]], replacing [[Kamil Grosicki]] for the last five minutes of the game.<ref>{{cite news |title=Angers – Rennes – Ligue 1 |url=http://www.eurosport.fr/football/ligue-1/2015-2016/live-sco-angers-stade-rennais_mtc782233/live.shtml |publisher=[[Eurosport]] |access-date=11 August 2017 |date=6 November 2015 |archive-date=11 August 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170811143258/http://www.eurosport.fr/football/ligue-1/2015-2016/live-sco-angers-stade-rennais_mtc782233/live.shtml |url-status=live }}</ref> On 22 November, he scored his first Ligue 1 goal for the first team against [[FC Girondins de Bordeaux|Bordeaux]], opening a 2–2 draw at [[Roazhon Park]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Crossan |first=D. |title=Carrasso saves point for Bordeaux |url=http://www.ligue1.com/ligue1/article/carrasso-saves-point-for-bordeaux.htm |publisher=[[Ligue 1]] |access-date=23 November 2015 |date=22 November 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151123083115/http://www.ligue1.com/ligue1/article/carrasso-saves-point-for-bordeaux.htm|archive-date=23 November 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 9 January 2016, Dembélé found the net again for Rennes, as they came from 0–2 down to draw 2–2 against regional rivals [[FC Lorient|Lorient]] at home.<ref>{{cite web |last=Gordon |first=Connor |title=Stade Rennais 2–2 FC Lorient: Hosts respond well after early derby disaster |url=https://www.vavel.com/en/football/2016/01/09/588841-stade-rennais-2-2-fc-lorient-hosts-respond-well-after-early-disaster.html |access-date=13 May 2016 |website=Vavel |date=9 January 2016 |archive-date=12 July 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180712120712/https://www.vavel.com/en/football/2016/01/09/588841-stade-rennais-2-2-fc-lorient-hosts-respond-well-after-early-disaster.html |url-status=live }}</ref> On 6 March, he scored his first Ligue 1 [[hat-trick]] in a 4–1 victory over [[FC Nantes|Nantes]] in the [[Derby Breton]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Ligue 1 : Rennes écrase Nantes (4–1) |url=http://www.lemonde.fr/ligue-1/article/2016/03/06/ligue-1-rennes-ecrase-nantes-4-0_4877505_1616940.html |work=[[Le Monde]] |date=6 March 2016 |access-date=11 August 2017 |language=fr |archive-date=11 August 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170811105001/http://www.lemonde.fr/ligue-1/article/2016/03/06/ligue-1-rennes-ecrase-nantes-4-0_4877505_1616940.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 18 March, he scored his tenth goal of the season in a 5–2 win against [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]] at the [[Stade Vélodrome]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lemonde.fr/ligue-1/article/2016/03/19/ligue-1-apres-sa-defaite-face-a-rennes-marseille-touche-le-fond_4886055_1616940.html|title=Ligue 1 : après sa défaite face à Rennes, Marseille touche le fond|language=French|date=19 March 2016|access-date=30 April 2025|website=Le Monde|archive-date=15 July 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250715153900/https://www.lemonde.fr/ligue-1/article/2016/03/19/ligue-1-apres-sa-defaite-face-a-rennes-marseille-touche-le-fond_4886055_1616940.html|url-status=live}}</ref> He ended his debut season with twelve goals from 29 matches, after scoring twice in a 3–1 win against [[Stade Reims]] on 2 April.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ouest-france.fr/sport/football/stade-rennais/en-direct/live-ligue-1-rennes-reims-4137935|title=Revivez la victoire du Stade Rennais 3–1 contre Reims|date=2 April 2016|access-date=30 April 2025|website=Ouest France|archive-date=10 August 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250810113617/https://www.ouest-france.fr/sport/football/stade-rennais/en-direct/live-ligue-1-rennes-reims-4137935|url-status=live}}</ref>

Rennes' sporting director [[Mikaël Silvestre]] compared Dembélé to [[Cristiano Ronaldo]], whom he had seen arrive at [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] around the same age.<ref name=france3/>

===Borussia Dortmund===
[[File:Dembele170727-2 (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|Dembele training with [[Borussia Dortmund]] in 2017]]

On 12 May 2016, Dembélé signed a five-year contract with German club [[Borussia Dortmund]], effective 1 July.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.bvb.de/eng/News/Overview/Borussia-Dortmund-signs-top-talent-Ousmane-Dembele |title=Borussia Dortmund signs top talent Ousmane Dembélé |publisher=[[Borussia Dortmund]] |date=12 May 2016 |access-date=12 May 2016 |archive-date=18 May 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160518002702/http://www.bvb.de/eng/News/Overview/Borussia-Dortmund-signs-top-talent-Ousmane-Dembele |url-status=live }}</ref> On 14 August, he made his debut in a 2–0 defeat against [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] in the [[2016 DFL-Supercup|DFL-Supercup]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.dfb.de/supercup/spielplan/?spieledb_path=%2Fmatches%2F2234139 |title=Deutscher Supercup, 2016, Finale |publisher=[[German Football Association]] |date=14 August 2016 |access-date=11 August 2017 |language=de |archive-date=20 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200620194359/https://www.dfb.de/supercup/spielplan/?spieledb_path=%2Fmatches%2F2234139 |url-status=live }}</ref> He scored his first goal for Dortmund on 20 September, in a [[Bundesliga]] encounter against [[VfL Wolfsburg]], which Dortmund won 5–1 at the [[Volkswagen Arena]].<ref>{{cite news |title=VfL Wolfsburg 1–5 Borussia Dortmund |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/37408762 |access-date=11 August 2017 |work=[[BBC Sport]] |date=20 September 2016 |archive-date=14 October 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201014164528/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/37408762 |url-status=live }}</ref> On 22 November, he scored the first [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] goal of his career as the German club defeated [[Legia Warsaw]] 8–4 in a group stage meeting.<ref>{{cite web |last=Uersfeld |first=Stephan |title=Borussia Dortmund 8–4 Legia Warsaw: Champions League record-breaker |url=http://www.espnfc.com/club/borussia-dortmund/124/blog/post/3002415/borussia-dortmund-8-legia-warsaw-4-champions-league-recordbreaker |website=[[ESPN FC]] |access-date=11 August 2017 |date=23 November 2016 |archive-date=13 October 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191013013003/http://www.espnfc.com/club/borussia-dortmund/124/blog/post/3002415/borussia-dortmund-8-legia-warsaw-4-champions-league-recordbreaker |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 26 April 2017, in the [[2016–17 DFB-Pokal|DFB-Pokal]] semi-final against Bayern Munich, Dembélé assisted [[Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang]]'s 69th-minute equaliser and scored the winning goal in the 74th minute, helping Dortmund reach the [[2017 DFB-Pokal Final]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Borussia Dortmund beat Bayern Munich to reach DFB Cup final – as it happened! |url=http://www.bundesliga.com/en/news/Bundesliga/bayern-munich-borussia-dortmund-dfb-cup-live-blog-lewandowski-aubameyang-pulisic-dembele-alaba-robben-blmd30n-441903.jsp |publisher=[[Bundesliga]] |access-date=11 August 2017 |date=26 April 2017 |archive-date=11 August 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170811182546/http://www.bundesliga.com/en/news/Bundesliga/bayern-munich-borussia-dortmund-dfb-cup-live-blog-lewandowski-aubameyang-pulisic-dembele-alaba-robben-blmd30n-441903.jsp |url-status=live }}</ref> On 27 May, in the decisive match against [[Eintracht Frankfurt]] at the [[Olympiastadion (Berlin)|Berlin Olympiastadion]], he scored the first goal of a 2–1 victory as Dortmund clinched their first major title in five years. Dembélé was subsequently named [[man of the match]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Buczko |first=Stefan |url=http://www.espnfc.com/club/borussia-dortmund/124/blog/post/3135170/ousmane-dembele-christian-pulisic-send-borussia-dortmund-from-title-drought-in-dfb-pokal-final |title=Dembele, Pulisic deliver Dortmund from title drought in DFB Pokal final |website=ESPN FC |date=28 May 2017 |access-date=8 June 2017 |archive-date=8 September 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180908082721/http://www.espnfc.com/club/borussia-dortmund/124/blog/post/3135170/ousmane-dembele-christian-pulisic-send-borussia-dortmund-from-title-drought-in-dfb-pokal-final |url-status=live }}</ref>

After scoring six goals and recording 13 assists during [[2016–17 Bundesliga|2016–17]], Dembélé was named to the Bundesliga Team of the Season and awarded the league's Rookie of the Season award.<ref name="ToS"/><ref name="RtS"/>

===Barcelona===
On 25 August 2017, [[La Liga]] side [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] announced that they had reached an agreement to sign Dembélé for €105&nbsp;million plus a reported €40&nbsp;million add-ons.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/41044659 |title=Ousmane Dembele: Barcelona agree £135.5m deal for Dortmund forward |date=25 August 2017 |access-date=25 August 2017 |work=BBC Sport |archive-date=25 August 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170825230601/http://www.bbc.com/sport/football/41044659 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Marsden |first=Samuel |url=http://www.espnfc.com.au/story/3188187/borussia-dortmund-confirm-barcelona-close-to-ousmane-dembele-deal |title=Borussia Dortmund confirm Barcelona close to Ousmane Dembele deal |date=25 August 2017 |access-date=25 August 2017 |website=ESPN FC |archive-date=25 August 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170825181927/http://www.espnfc.com.au/story/3188187/borussia-dortmund-confirm-barcelona-close-to-ousmane-dembele-deal |url-status=live }}</ref> On 28 August, he had his medical and signed a five-year contract, with his [[buyout clause]] set at €400&nbsp;million.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/press-release-ousmane-dembele-fcbarcelona-signing |title=Ousmane Dembélé, FC Barcelona's new signing |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=25 August 2017 |access-date=25 August 2017 |archive-date=22 June 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210622080452/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/748188/ousmane-dembele-fc-barcelonas-new-signing |url-status=live }}</ref> Barcelona had sold [[Neymar]] to [[Paris Saint-Germain FC|Paris Saint-Germain]] (PSG) for €222&nbsp;million, so the deal meant that Dembélé became the [[List of most expensive association football transfers|joint-second most expensive player (in euros)]], along with [[Paul Pogba]]. Rennes received a reported €20&nbsp;million from Borussia Dortmund as a result of the sale,<ref>{{cite web |last=Bushnell |first=Henry |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/barcelona-signs-ousmane-dembele-neymar-replacement-ways-one-154647028.html |title=Barcelona signs Ousmane Dembele, its Neymar replacement in more ways than one |website=[[Yahoo Sports]] |date=25 August 2017 |access-date=25 August 2017 |archive-date=25 August 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170825234919/https://sports.yahoo.com/barcelona-signs-ousmane-dembele-neymar-replacement-ways-one-154647028.html |url-status=live }}</ref> and Évreux 27 were also due part of the fee.<ref name=evreux/> He was handed the number 11 shirt previously worn by Neymar.<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.si.com/soccer/2017/08/25/barcelona-hand-ousmane-dembele-number-11-shirt-following-record-move-dortmund |title=Barcelona Hands Ousmane Dembele Neymar's No. 11 Shirt After Dortmund Transfer |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=25 August 2017 |access-date=8 September 2017 |archive-date=3 September 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170903165159/https://www.si.com/soccer/2017/08/25/barcelona-hand-ousmane-dembele-number-11-shirt-following-record-move-dortmund |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite tweet|author=FC Barcelona |user=FCBarcelona |number=901101904419311616 |title=The shirt number for @Dembouz is… |date=25 August 2017 |access-date=25 August 2017}}</ref>

====2017–18: First season and domestic double====
Dembélé made his debut on 9 September as a 68th-minute substitute for [[Gerard Deulofeu]] in a 5–0 [[Derbi barceloní]] win over [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]] at the [[Camp Nou]], assisting the final goal by [[Luis Suárez (Uruguayan footballer)|Luis Suárez]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Emons |first=Michael |title=Barcelona 5–0 Espanyol |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/41212266 |access-date=9 September 2017 |work=BBC Sport |date=9 September 2017 |archive-date=19 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180619115724/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/41212266 |url-status=live }}</ref> In his first league start eight days later at [[Getafe CF|Getafe]], he injured his hamstring and was ruled out for four months.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/ousmane-dembele-medical-announcement |title=Ousmane Dembélé medical announcement |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=17 September 2017 |access-date=15 March 2018 |archive-date=11 March 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180311182314/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/ousmane-dembele-medical-announcement |url-status=live }}</ref> He was given the medical all-clear on 2 January 2018,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/ousmane-dembele-receives-medical-discharge|title=Ousmane Dembélé receives medical discharge|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=2 January 2018|access-date=15 January 2018|archive-date=5 January 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180105184309/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/ousmane-dembele-receives-medical-discharge|url-status=live}}</ref> but a couple weeks later, he again injured himself against [[Real Sociedad]] and was ruled out for up to four weeks.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/dembele-out-for-three-to-four-weeks-injury-news-fcbarcelona |title=Dembélé out for three to four weeks |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=15 January 2018 |access-date=15 January 2018 |archive-date=16 January 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180116011140/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/dembele-out-for-three-to-four-weeks-injury-news-fcbarcelona |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 14 March 2018, Dembélé scored his first goal for Barcelona, netting the second goal in a 3–0 second leg win in the [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] round of 16 against [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Lowe |first=Sid |author-link=Sid Lowe |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2018/mar/14/barcelona-chelsea-champions-league-ousmane-dembele-lionel-messi |title=Ousmane Dembélé finally shines but the night belongs to Lionel Messi |date=14 March 2018 |access-date=14 March 2018 |newspaper=The Guardian |archive-date=22 April 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180422213307/https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2018/mar/14/barcelona-chelsea-champions-league-ousmane-dembele-lionel-messi |url-status=live }}</ref> On 17 April, he scored his first La Liga goal, the opening goal in an eventual 2–2 draw with [[RC Celta de Vigo|Celta Vigo]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/43779070 |title=Celta Vigo 2–2 Barcelona |date=17 April 2018 |work=BBC Sport |access-date=5 September 2018 |archive-date=6 September 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180906024147/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/43779070 |url-status=live }}</ref> On 9 May, Dembélé scored twice, marking the first brace of his Barcelona career, in a 5–1 home victory over [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44024612 |title=Barcelona 5–1 Villarreal |date=9 May 2018 |work=BBC Sport |access-date=5 September 2018 |archive-date=17 August 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180817234127/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44024612 |url-status=live }}</ref> Dembélé won both the [[Copa del Rey]] and La Liga winners' medals in his first season in Spain, with the 20-year-old scoring four goals in 24 appearances across all competitions.<ref name=1718season/>

====2018–19: Supercopa de España and second La Liga title====
[[File:Ousmane Dembélé vs Valladolid 2.jpg|thumb|upright|Dembélé playing for [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] in 2018]]

On 12 August 2018, Dembélé scored the winning goal against [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] in the [[2018 Supercopa de España|Supercopa de España]], in an eventual 2–1 victory to win Barcelona their 13th [[Supercopa de España]] title.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/45164525 |title=Barcelona beat Sevilla 2–1 to win Spanish Super Cup in Morocco |date=12 August 2018 |work=BBC Sport |access-date=13 August 2018 |archive-date=31 August 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180831213542/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/45164525 |url-status=live }}</ref> He opened his [[2018–19 La Liga|La Liga season]]'s goal tally by scoring the only goal of the game against [[Real Valladolid]], on 25 August, away at the [[Estadio José Zorrilla]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/45311759 |title=Real Valladolid 0–1 Barcelona: Champions win after VAR reprieve |date=25 August 2018 |work=BBC Sport |access-date=27 August 2018 |archive-date=26 August 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180826212355/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/45311759 |url-status=live }}</ref> On 18 September, Dembélé scored his first Champions League goal of [[2018–19 UEFA Champions League|the season]], helping Barcelona beat [[PSV Eindhoven|PSV]] 4–0 at the Camp Nou.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.espn.com/soccer/report?gameId=526507 |title=Lionel Messi sets Champions League hat-trick record as Barcelona ease past PSV |website=[[ESPN.com]] |date=18 September 2018 |access-date=18 September 2018 |archive-date=18 September 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180918211539/http://www.espn.com/soccer/report?gameId=526507 |url-status=live }}</ref> On 4 November, he inspired Barcelona to a 3–2 comeback away against [[Rayo Vallecano]], scoring the 2–2 equaliser with a half-volley in the 87th minute.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://global.espn.com/football/report?gameId=521815 |title=Luis Suarez goal completes late comeback, puts Barcelona four points clear |date=4 November 2018 |publisher=ESPN |agency=Reuters |access-date=4 November 2018 |archive-date=4 November 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181104050236/http://global.espn.com/football/report?gameId=521815 |url-status=live }}</ref> On 11 December, he scored a remarkable solo goal against [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] outpacing many defenders, finishing with a cool left footed shot past [[Hugo Lloris]]. He won the UEFA Champions League Goal of the Week for that goal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/942542/dembele-awarded-goal-of-the-week|title=Dembélé awarded 'Goal of the Week'|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=14 December 2018|access-date=10 July 2021|archive-date=10 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210710145006/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/942542/dembele-awarded-goal-of-the-week|url-status=live}}</ref> After the match, Barcelona manager [[Ernesto Valverde]] praised the youngster, saying "He has made a great goal, within reach of players with his talent."<ref>{{cite news |url=https://en.as.com/en/2018/12/12/football/1544617844_632562.html |title=Dembélé stunner against Spurs pleases Barça boss Valverde |date=12 December 2018 |newspaper=[[Diario AS]] |access-date=11 January 2019 |archive-date=28 November 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201128052436/https://en.as.com/en/2018/12/12/football/1544617844_632562.html |url-status=live }}</ref> He finished the season with 14 goals, 8 of them in the league, as his club managed to win another La Liga title.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.goal.com/en-tza/news/ousmane-dembele-injury-history-barcelona-france-how-many-games-missed/bltd9fa9952c628b116 |title=Ousmane Dembele injury history: Barcelona & France star's absences & how many games he has missed |publisher=Goal.com |date=26 January 2022 |access-date=11 August 2023 |archive-date=11 August 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230811015901/https://www.goal.com/en-tza/news/ousmane-dembele-injury-history-barcelona-france-how-many-games-missed/bltd9fa9952c628b116 |url-status=live }}</ref>

====2019–21: Recurring injuries====
Dembélé injured his left hamstring in the opening match of the [[2019–20 La Liga|2019–20 La Liga season]], a 0–1 defeat against [[Athletic Bilbao]], and was expected to miss five weeks.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.lesportiudecatalunya.cat/barca/article/1652741-dembele-es-torna-a-trencar-i-sera-baixa-cinc-setmanes.html|title=Dembélé es torna a trencar i serà baixa cinc setmanes|last=Fibla|first=Albert|date=20 August 2019|work=[[L'Esportiu]]|language=ca|access-date=20 August 2019|archive-date=20 August 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190820044437/https://www.lesportiudecatalunya.cat/barca/article/1652741-dembele-es-torna-a-trencar-i-sera-baixa-cinc-setmanes.html|url-status=live}}</ref> He returned as a half-time substitute in Barcelona's 2–1 home win over Villarreal on 24 September. He scored his first goal of the season in a 4–0 win over Sevilla on 6 October, but was later sent off for dissent.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/barcelona/opinion/2019/10/07/5d9a61f922601d0d558b461a.html|title=Dembélé y su desquiciante lado oscuro|language=Spanish|date=7 October 2019|access-date=30 April 2025|website=Marca|archive-date=19 December 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221219205636/https://www.marca.com/futbol/barcelona/opinion/2019/10/07/5d9a61f922601d0d558b461a.html|url-status=live}}</ref> On 27 November, in a [[2019–20 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] [[2019–20 UEFA Champions League group stage|group]] match against his former club Borussia Dortmund, Dembélé suffered an injury which led to his substitution after 24 minutes.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.as.com/en/2019/11/27/soccer/1574887249_633144.html|title=Distraught Ousmane Dembélé forced off with injury|date=27 November 2019|access-date=30 April 2025|website=AS|archive-date=20 March 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250320094110/https://en.as.com/en/2019/11/27/soccer/1574887249_633144.html|url-status=live}}</ref> It was later confirmed by Barcelona that he would miss the following ten weeks with a thigh injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/50606908|title=Ousmane Dembele: Barcelona winger out for 10 weeks with thigh injury|date=29 November 2019|access-date=30 April 2025|website=BBC Sport|archive-date=11 March 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250311181101/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/50606908|url-status=live}}</ref>

In February 2020, on his return to training, he suffered a serious hamstring tear which ended his season.<ref>{{cite news |title=Ousmane Dembele: Barcelona winger sidelined for six months after surgery |work=BBC Sport |date=11 February 2020 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51467123 |access-date=12 February 2020 |archive-date=12 February 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200212150137/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51467123 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/barcelona/2020/02/04/5e396af946163f47848b45e2.html|title=Grave lesión de Dembélé: se pierde lo que queda de temporada|language=Spanish|date=4 February 2020|access-date=30 April 2025|website=Marca|archive-date=19 April 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240419124925/https://www.marca.com/futbol/barcelona/2020/02/04/5e396af946163f47848b45e2.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

Dembélé returned to the field for the first time in ten months as a 70th-minute substitute for [[Ansu Fati]] in Barcelona's [[2020–21 La Liga|La Liga]] fixture against Villarreal on 27 September 2020.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1845877/fc-barcelona-v-villarreal-four-midable-4-0|title=FC Barcelona v Villarreal: Four-midable (4–0)|date=27 September 2020|access-date=30 April 2025|website=FC Barcelona|archive-date=9 May 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250509113644/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1845877/fc-barcelona-v-villarreal-four-midable-4-0|url-status=live}}</ref> He scored his first goal in 380 days in the team's first [[2020–21 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] fixture of the [[2020–21 FC Barcelona season|season]] against [[Ferencváros]] on 20 October.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/2020/10/20/champions/1603215126_595016.html|title=Barcelona 5 – Ferencvaros 1: resumen, resultado y goles|language=Spanish|date=21 October 2020|access-date=30 April 2025|website=AS|archive-date=25 March 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240325172247/https://as.com/futbol/2020/10/20/champions/1603215126_595016.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

====2021–23: Hamstring surgery and La Liga assist leader====
Dembélé suffered a hamstring injury when playing with France national team in the delayed [[UEFA Euro 2020]] in 2021. His injury required surgery, and was operated on in [[Turku]], Finland, by surgeon Lasse Lempainen in late June 2021.<ref>[https://www.iltalehti.fi/jalkapallon-em-2021/a/15d7542c-d33a-44f1-8cd7-ebc3d201907e 125 miljoonan euron mies leikattiin Turussa: tähtipelaajan EM-kisat jäivät kesken – ”Päätös oli selkeä”], [[Iltalehti]], 29 June 2021</ref><ref>[https://www.ts.fi/urheilu/5356345 Ousmane Dembele leikattiin maanantaina Turussa – ranskalaishyökkääjällä edessään neljän kuukauden kuntoutuminen] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240106192752/https://www.ts.fi/urheilu/5356345 |date=6 January 2024 }}, [[Turun Sanomat]], 29 June 2021</ref> Dembélé was also operated on by Lempainen and [[Sakari Orava]] in 2017 and 2020.<ref>[https://www.hs.fi/urheilu/art-2000008090026.html Ranskalaistähti Ousmane Dembélé kävi taas Turussa leikkauksessa: ”Takareiden totaalinen jännerepeämä”] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240106192752/https://www.hs.fi/urheilu/art-2000008090026.html |date=6 January 2024 }}, [[Helsingin Sanomat]], 29 June 2021</ref><ref>[https://www.satakunnankansa.fi/urheilu/art-2000008375158.html Vammakierre poikki] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240107115233/https://www.satakunnankansa.fi/urheilu/art-2000008375158.html |date=7 January 2024 }}, [[Satakunnan Kansa]], 2 November 2021</ref>

On 10 May 2022, Dembélé provided two assists in a 3–1 home victory over Celta Vigo. It was his 10th and 11th league assists in 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2612999/two-more-assists-for-dembele|title=Two more assists for Dembélé|website=FC Barcelona|date=10 May 2022|accessdate=25 May 2022|archive-date=25 May 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220525185451/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2612999/two-more-assists-for-dembele|url-status=live}}</ref> He finished the [[2021–22 La Liga]] season as the league's top playmaker with thirteen assists.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.laliga.com/en-GB/leaderboard/all-leaders?stat_competition=laliga-santander&stat=total_assists_ranking|title=All leaders in Assists|access-date=23 September 2021|publisher=La Liga|archive-date=26 September 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200926053836/https://www.laliga.com/en-GB/leaderboard/all-leaders?stat_competition=laliga-santander&stat=total_assists_ranking|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 14 July 2022, Dembélé extended his contract with Barcelona until 30 June 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dembélé to sign contract until 2024 |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2672243/dembele-to-sign-contract-until-2024 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220714132724/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2672243/dembele-to-sign-contract-until-2024 |archive-date=14 July 2022 |access-date=15 July 2022 |website=FC Barcelona |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Ousmane Dembélé: 'FC Barcelona was always my first choice' |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2677465/ousmane-dembele-fc-barcelona-was-always-my-first-choice |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220714133613/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2677465/ousmane-dembele-fc-barcelona-was-always-my-first-choice |archive-date=14 July 2022 |access-date=15 July 2022 |website=FC Barcelona |language=en}}</ref> His release clause was set to €50 million, and later raised to €100 million on 1 August 2023.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.goal.com/en/news/psg-trigger-ousmane-dembele-private-eur50m-release-clause-barcelona/blt4214c1d891f87071 |title=PSG trigger Ousmane Dembele's 'private' €50m release clause with transfer from Barcelona set to be finalised this week |publisher=Goal.com |date=1 August 2023 |access-date=10 April 2024 |archive-date=15 August 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240815191458/https://www.goal.com/en/news/psg-trigger-ousmane-dembele-private-eur50m-release-clause-barcelona/blt4214c1d891f87071 |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Paris Saint-Germain===
==== 2023–24: First season in Paris and domestic double ====

|url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/story/_/id/38106043/psg-sign-dembele-barcelona-agreeing-50m-deal |title=PSG sign Dembele from Barcelona after agreeing €50m deal |publisher=ESPN |date=12 August web |date=12 August 2023 |title=Agreement on transfer of Ousmane Dembélé to Paris St Germain |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/3611320/agreement-on-transfer-of-ousmane-dembele-to-paris-st-germain |access-date=12 August 2023 |website=FC Barcelona |archive-date=14 November 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251114030401/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/3611320/agreement-on-transfer-of-ousmane-dembele-to-paris-st-germain |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Sanderson |first=Tom |title=FC Barcelona Come Out Of Dembele PSG Transfer Richer Than Expected After Pressuring Player's Camp: Reports |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/tomsanderson/2023/08/12/fc-barcelona-come-out-of-dembele-psg-transfer-richer-than-expected-after-pressuring-players-camp-reports/ |access-date=14 August 2023 |website=Forbes |archive-date=14 August 2023 |url-status=live }}</ref> He was initially assigned the number 23 jersey, but switched to the number 10 following Neymar's departure from the club.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |date=12 August 2023 |title=Ousmane Dembélé, another star in Paris |url=https://en.psg.fr/teams/first-team/content/ousmane-dembele-another-star-in-paris-psg-mercato-2324-equipe-premiere |access-date=12 August 2023 |website=Paris Saint-Germain FC |language=en }}{{Dead link|date=September 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref><ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=DEMB10UZ – The number 10 for Dembélé! April 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250425122551/https://en.psg.fr/teams/first-team/content/the-number-10-for-dembele-psg-paris-saint-germain |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On 20 August, Dembélé made his PSG debut, coming on as a substitute in a 1–1 draw away to [[Toulouse FC|Toulouse]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=19 August 2023 |title=Debut for Ousmane Dembélé |url=https://en.psg.fr/teams/first-team/content/debut-for-ousmane-dembele-toulouse-fc-paris-saint-germain-ligue-1-2023-2024 |access-date=20 August 2023 |publisher=Paris Saint-Germain FC |language=en On 24 September, he got his first goal involvement for PSG, providing the assist for [[Gonçalo Ramos]]'s first goal in a 4–0 [[Le Classique]] win over [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=24 September 2023 |title=Kolo Muani and Ramos score maiden PSG goals in win over Marseille |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/kolo-muani-ramos-score-maiden-psg-goals-win-over-marseille-2023-09-24/ |access-date=25 September 2023 |publisher=Reuters |archive-date=17 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231017134230/https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/kolo-muani-ramos-score-maiden-psg-goals-win-over-marseille-2023-09-24/ |url-status=live }}</ref> On 24 November, Dembélé scored his first goal for the club in a 5–2 win at home over [[AS Monaco FC|Monaco]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-11-24 |title=PSG feasts thanks to the rhythm of Dembélé and Mbappe |url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/ligue-1/2023/11/24/65610f8746163fb37f8b45d5.html |access-date=2023-11-24 |website=MARCA |language=en |archive-date=5 July 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260705081027/https://www.marca.com/en/football/ligue-1/2023/11/24/65610f8746163fb37f8b45d5.html |url-status=live }}</ref> On 10 April 2024, he scored his first Champions League goal with PSG in a 3–2 home defeat against his former club Barcelona in the quarter-final first leg.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68773222 |title=Paris Saint Germain 2–3 Barcelona |publisher=BBC Sport |date=10 April 2024 |access-date=10 April 2024 |archive-date=14 August 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250814223253/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68773222 |url-status=live }}</ref> In the second leg six days later, he scored PSG's first goal in a 4–1 away victory, helping secure his club's qualification to the semi-finals and taking home the player of the match award.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2024-04-16 |title=Barcelona vs PSG live updates |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/live-blogs/barcelona-psg-live-updates-champions-league-score-result/4v9YwEnKtuDz/ |access-date=2024-04-17 |website=The Athletic |language=en |archive-date=19 |url-status=live }}</ref> At the end of the [[2023–24 Ligue 1|2023–24 season]], Dembélé won the Ligue 1 title with PSG.<ref name="psg teams">{{Cite web |date=2024-04-28 |title=Paris Saint-Germain win their 12th Ligue 1 title! |url=https://en.psg.fr/teams/first-team/content/paris-saint-germain-win-their-12th-ligue-1-title-psg-ligue-1-club-2023-2024 |access-date=2025-01-29 |website=EN.PSG.FR He also scored the opening goal in PSG's 2–1 win over [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]] in the [[2024 Coupe de France final]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-05-25 |title=Paris Saint-Germain win the Coupe de France for the 15th time |url=https://en.psg.fr/teams/first-team/content/paris-saint-germain-win-the-coupe-de-france-for-the-15th-time-olympique-lyonnais-2023-2024 |access-date=2025-01-29 ==== 2024–25: Continental treble win and individual accolades ====
[[File:Paris Saint-Germain - Manchester City FC, 22 January 2025 (1069) (cropped).jpg|thumb|Dembélé playing for [[Paris Saint-Germain FC|Paris Saint-Germain]] in 2025]]

On 5 January 2025, Dembélé scored a stoppage-time winner as PSG defeated [[AS Monaco FC|Monaco]] 1–0 in the [[2024 Trophée des Champions]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-01-05 |title=Dembélé scores last-gasp winner as PSG wins Champions Trophy, Marseille routs Le Havre in Ligue 1 |url=https://apnews.com/article/psg-monaco-champions-trophy-marseille-ligue-1-c8282ad0234a33a3951db48f37fd7225 January, he scored Paris's first goal in a 4–2 comeback victory over [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] in the Champions League.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-01-22 |title=Joao Neves, Ousmane Dembele inspire PSG in epic 4–2 UEFA Champions League fightback win vs. Manchester City |language=en}}</ref> On 29 January, he scored a hat-trick in a 4–1 Champions League victory over [[VfB Stuttgart]], his second career hat-trick and first in European competitions, helping PSG qualify to the [[2024–25 UEFA Champions League knockout phase#Knockout phase play-offs|knockout phase play-offs]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-01-29 |title=Ousmane Dembélé completes second career hat trick at right time for PSG |url=https://apnews.com/article/psg-dembele-hat-trick-89bf43d8d42c5299b650d809bc4258e6 |access-date=2025-01-29 |website=AP News |language=en |archive-date=29 January 2025 another hat-trick in a 5–2 league win away to [[Stade Brestois 29|Brest]], becoming the first PSG player to have scored consecutive hat-tricks in official matches.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= Dembélé ended the season as joint-top scorer in Ligue 1 with 21 goals, having helped PSG to their 13th league title.<ref name="lequipe 1">{{cite web |title=D'abord mené, le PSG termine la saison par une victoire à domicile contre Auxerre |url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/D-abord-mene-le-psg-termine-la-saison-par-une-victoire-a-domicile-contre-auxerre/1562626 |website=L’Équipe |access-date=18 May 2025 |archive-date=29 November 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251129211001/https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/D-abord-mene-le-psg-termine-la-saison-par-une-victoire-a-domicile-contre-auxerre/1562626 |url-status=live }}</ref> He was also named the [[Ligue 1 Player of the Year]] for the first time, and was included in the Ligue 1 Team of the Year.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |title=Ousmane Dembélé élu meilleur joueur de Ligue 1 pour la première fois aux Trophées UNFP |url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Ousmane-dembele-elu-meilleur-joueur-de-ligue-1-pour-la-premiere-fois-aux-trophees-unfp/1561044 |access-date=2025-05-11 |website=L'Équipe |language=fr |archive-date=23 September 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250923081656/https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Ousmane-dembele-elu-meilleur-joueur-de-ligue-1-pour-la-premiere-fois-aux-trophees-unfp/1561044 |url-status=live }}</ref> On 31 May 2025, Dembélé won the Champions League after PSG beat [[Inter Milan]] 5–0 in [[2025 UEFA Champions League final|the final]], a match in which he provided two assists.<ref>{{Cite web |last=CHOSUNBIZ |date=2025-06-01 |title=Dembélé shines with two assists as PSG wins UCL final; Enrique backs Ballon d'Or candidacy |url=https://biz.chosun.com/en/en-sports/2025/06/01/7WVP25H7TBEXDBTWGE6DSQIF5M/ |access-date=2025-06-02 |website=CHOSUNBIZ |language=en |archive-date=10 August 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250810113635/https://biz.chosun.com/en/en-sports/2025/06/01/7WVP25H7TBEXDBTWGE6DSQIF5M/ |url-status=live }}</ref> After the final, his statistics for the season were of 33 goals and 15 assists in 49 appearances in all competitions,<ref>{{Cite web |date=1 June 2025 |title=Dembele Wins UEFA Champions League Player of the Season Award |url=https://qna.org.qa/en/news/news-details?id=dembele-wins-uefa-champions-league-player-of-the-season-award&date=1/06/2025#:~:text=He%20scored%2033%20goals%20%2D%2021,one%20in%20the%20French%20Cup. |access-date=1 June 2025 |website=qna.org.qa}}</ref> leading to him being cited as one of the leading candidates for the [[2025 Ballon d'Or]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=McVitie |first=Peter |date=May 31, 2025 |title='Given us all a slap in the face!' – Ex-Barcelona chief lifts lid on Ousmane Dembele's exit for PSG and says Ballon d'Or hopeful has 'taught us a lesson' |url=https://www.goal.com/en/lists/slap-in-face-barcelona-chief-ousmane-dembele-exit-psg-star-taught-a-lesson/bltb5d0b83c0e02c262 |access-date=2025-06-01 |website=[[Goal.com]] |archive-date=1 June 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250601084720/https://www.goal.com/en/lists/slap-in-face-barcelona-chief-ousmane-dembele-exit-psg-star-taught-a-lesson/bltb5d0b83c0e02c262 |url-status=live }}</ref> which he ultimately won.<ref name=":9" /> At the [[2025 FIFA Club World Cup]], after missing the group stage due to injury, Dembélé scored a goal in a 2–0 win over Bayern Munich in the quarter-finals and recorded a goal and assist in a 4–0 win over [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in the semi-finals. PSG went on to finish as runners-up following a 3–0 final defeat to Chelsea.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-07-13 |title=Paris lose to Chelsea |url=https://www.psg.fr/en/content/match-report-paris-saint-germain-lose-to-chelsea-fc-fifa-club-world-cup-2025 |access-date=2025-07-14 |website=www.psg.fr |language=en |archive-date=3 August 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250803060513/https://www.psg.fr/en/content/match-report-paris-saint-germain-lose-to-chelsea-fc-fifa-club-world-cup-2025 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==== 2025–26: Back-to-back Champions League titles ====
Dembélé won the [[UEFA Super Cup]] with PSG on 13 August, scoring in a 4–3 penalty shoot-out after [[2025 UEFA Super Cup|a 2–2 draw]] against [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]]. His stoppage-time assist for [[Gonçalo Ramos]]'s header and his successful penalty in the shoot-out were among the contributions that earned him the Player of the Match award.<ref>{{Cite web |date=13 August 2025 |title=Ousmane Dembélé named 2025 UEFA Super Cup Player of the Match |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefasupercup/news/029c-1e7902cb3f22-a51ae8a63eaa-1000--ousmane-dembele-named-2025-uefa-super-cup-player-of-the-/ |access-date=13 August 2025 |website=[[UEFA]]}}</ref> On 30 August 2025, Dembélé scored his first two goals of the season, two penalties in a 6–3 win away to [[Toulouse FC|Toulouse]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-08-30 |title=João Neves and Paris put on a show at the Stadium! |url=https://www.psg.fr/en/content/joao-neves-and-paris-put-on-a-show-at-the-stadium-match-report-toulouse-fc-paris-saint-germain-ligue-1-20252026 |access-date=2025-08-30 |website=www.psg.fr |language=en |archive-date=30 August 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250830230024/https://www.psg.fr/en/content/joao-neves-and-paris-put-on-a-show-at-the-stadium-match-report-toulouse-fc-paris-saint-germain-ligue-1-20252026 |url-status=live }}</ref> but while on international duty in early September, he suffered a hamstring injury that would keep him out of action for six weeks.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-09-06 |title=Source: PSG irate over Dembélé injury with France |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/46174602/psg-angry-france-didier-deschamps-ousmane-dembele-injury |access-date=2025-09-10 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> That same month, he won the 2025 Ballon d'Or.<ref name=":9">{{Cite web |title=Ballon d'Or 2025 LIVE: Winners, times & updates from ceremony in Paris |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cdr6kzzlzn0t |access-date=2025-09-22 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB |archive-date=22 September 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250922230819/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cdr6kzzlzn0t |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 22 October, Dembélé returned from injury for PSG, scoring in a 7–2 victory over [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]] in the Champions League.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=Ousmane Dembélé Happy After His PSG Return: "I Came Back Quietly" |url-status=live }}</ref> On 4 November, in a match against Bayern Munich, he suffered another injury, this time to the calf, keeping him out of action for "several weeks."<ref>{{Cite web triumphs over Olympique de Marseille: goals and drama all the way to penalties in the Trophée des Champions |url=https://www.beinsports.com/en-us/soccer/trophe-des-champions/articles/paris-saint-germain-triumphs-over-olympique-de-marseille-goals-and-drama-all-the-way-to-penalties-in-the-troph%C3%A9e-des-champions-2026-01-08 |access-date=2026-01-17 |website=beIN SPORTS |language=en-us |archive-date=8 January 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260108221143/https://www.beinsports.com/en-us/soccer/trophe-des-champions/articles/paris-saint-germain-triumphs-over-olympique-de-marseille-goals-and-drama-all-the-way-to-penalties-in-the-troph%C3%A9e-des-champions-2026-01-08 |url-status=live }}</ref> On 14 April, he scored twice in a 2–0 away victory against Liverpool in the [[2025–26 UEFA Champions League knockout phase|Champions League quarter-final]] second leg, sealing progression to the semi-finals with a 4–0 aggregate win.<ref>{{cite web |last=Patel |first=Aadam |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c4g89qene45t |title=Liverpool 0–2 Paris Saint-Germain |publisher=BBC Sport |date=14 April 2026 |access-date=14 April 2026 |archive-date=14 April 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260414194243/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c4g89qene45t |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 11 May, Dembélé was named the [[Trophées UNFP du football|UNFP]] [[Ligue 1 Player of the Year]] for the second consecutive season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ousmane Dembélé, Pierre Sage, Zouriko Davitashvili, Melchie Dumornay, Michael Olise... Le palmarès complet des trophées UNFP 2025–2026 |url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Ousmane-dembele-pierre-sage-zouriko-davitachvili-melchie-dumornay-michael-olise-le-palmares-complet-des-trophees-unfp-2025-2026/1675099 |access-date=2026-05-12 |website=L'Équipe |language=fr |archive-date=13 May 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260513140042/https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Ousmane-dembele-pierre-sage-zouriko-davitachvili-melchie-dumornay-michael-olise-le-palmares-complet-des-trophees-unfp-2025-2026/1675099 |url-status=live }}</ref> He became only the fifth player in the history of the award to win in back-to-back years, joining a list that includes [[Zlatan Ibrahimović]] and [[Kylian Mbappé]]. Despite a season interrupted by injuries, he finished the domestic campaign with 10 goals and 6 assists, playing a pivotal role in [[Paris Saint-Germain FC|Paris Saint-Germain]] securing their 12th league title in 14 years.<ref>{{Cite web |title=PSG's Dembele named UNFP Ligue 1 Player of the Year again |url=https://www.thescore.com/fra_fed/news/3539245 |access-date=2026-05-12 |website=thescore.com |language=en}}</ref> Later that month, on 30 May, he scored the equalising penalty in a 1–1 draw against [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] in the [[2026 UEFA Champions League final|UEFA Champions League final]], before Paris Saint-Germain prevailed 4–3 in the penalty shootout to retain the trophy.<ref>{{cite web |last=Howell |first=Alex |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cj6ppx48pk2t |title=Paris Saint-Germain 1–1 Arsenal (4–3 on pens) |publisher=BBC Sport |date=30 May 2026 |access-date=30 May 2026 |archive-date=6 July 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260706053910/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cj6ppx48pk2t |url-status=live }}</ref>

==International career==
[[File:Ousmane Dembélé World Cup Trophy.jpg|thumb|upright|Dembélé after winning the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]] with [[France national football team|France]]|left]]

Dembélé was called up to the senior [[France national football team|France]] squad for the first time in August 2016 to face [[Italy national football team|Italy]] and [[Belarus national football team|Belarus]] in [[Exhibition game|friendlies]] after [[Alexandre Lacazette]] and [[Nabil Fekir]] withdrew through injury.<ref>{{cite news|title=Dembélé, Gameiro et Kondogbia appelés chez les Bleus|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Dembele-gameiro-et-kondogbia-appeles-chez-les-bleus/722124|work=[[L'Équipe]]|date=29 August 2016|access-date=29 August 2016|language=fr|archive-date=31 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160831174918/http://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Dembele-gameiro-et-kondogbia-appeles-chez-les-bleus/722124|url-status=live}}</ref> He made his debut on 1 September against the former at the [[Stadio San Nicola]], replacing [[Antoine Griezmann]] for the final 27 minutes of a 3–1 win.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.espnfc.us/report?gameId=460628 |title=Italy vs. France |website=ESPN FC |date=2 September 2016 |access-date=11 August 2017 |archive-date=21 August 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170821125345/http://www.espnfc.us/report?gameId=460628 |url-status=live }}</ref> On 13 June 2017, Dembélé scored his first goal for France in a 3–2 friendly victory against [[England national football team|England]].<ref>{{cite news |last=McNulty |first=Phil |author-link=Phil McNulty |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40168358 |title=France 3–2 England |publisher=BBC Sport |date=13 June 2017 |access-date=11 August 2017 |archive-date=20 October 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181020184417/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40168358 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 17 May 2018, Dembélé was named in the 23-man French squad for the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]] in Russia.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/12025/11376691/alexandre-lacazette-and-anthony-martial-on-standby-for-france-world-cup-squad-and-dimitri-payet-out |title=Alexandre Lacazette and Anthony Martial on standby for France World Cup squad and Dimitri Payet out |date=21 May 2018 |work=[[Sky Sports]] |last=Charles |first=Andy |access-date=21 May 2018 |archive-date=27 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190327191937/https://www.skysports.com/football/news/12025/11376691/alexandre-lacazette-and-anthony-martial-on-standby-for-france-world-cup-squad-and-dimitri-payet-out |url-status=live }}</ref> He featured in four matches during the tournament, including all group stage matches and appearing as a late substitute in the quarter-final against [[Uruguay national football team|Uruguay]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.dw.com/en/world-cup-2018-varane-header-and-muslera-howler-sends-france-into-last-four/a-44554278 |title=World Cup 2018: France ease past Uruguay to reach last four |publisher=DW |date=6 July 2018 |access-date=27 June 2026 |archive-date=30 July 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240730183926/https://www.dw.com/en/world-cup-2018-varane-header-and-muslera-howler-sends-france-into-last-four/a-44554278 |url-status=live }}</ref> On 15 July, he was an unused substitute as France beat [[Croatia national football team|Croatia]] 4–2 in the [[2018 FIFA World Cup final|final]].<ref name="WC2018">{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44754965 |title=France 4–2 Croatia |first=Phil |last=McNulty |publisher=BBC Sport |date=15 July 2018 |access-date=18 December 2022 |archive-date=25 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190325011256/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44754965 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 18 May 2021, Dembélé was selected in the French squad for the postponed [[UEFA Euro 2020]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/La-liste-des-26-bleus-de-didier-deschamps-pour-l-euro-2021-avec-benzema-kounde-et-thuram-mais-sans-martial-ni-camavinga-eg/1253582 |title=La liste des 26 Bleus de Didier Deschamps pour l'Euro 2021 : avec Benzema, Koundé et Thuram, mais sans Martial ni Camavinga |publisher=L'Équipe |language=fr |date=18 May 2021 |access-date=27 June 2026 |archive-date=18 July 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260718130950/https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/La-liste-des-26-bleus-de-didier-deschamps-pour-l-euro-2021-avec-benzema-kounde-et-thuram-mais-sans-martial-ni-camavinga-eg/1253582 |url-status=live }}</ref> In the second group stage match against [[Hungary national football team|Hungary]], he sustained a rupture of the right hamstring tendon at the knee level which ruled him out for the remainder of the tournament.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.eurosport.fr/football/euro-2020/2021/euro-2020-ousmane-dembele-forfait-pour-la-fin-du-tournoi-quitte-le-rassemblement-des-bleus_sto8384062/story.shtml |title=Euro 2020 - Ousmane Dembélé, forfait pour la fin du tournoi, quitte le rassemblement des Bleus |publisher=Eurosport |language=fr |date=21 June 2021 }}</ref>

Dembélé was called up to the French squad for the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]] in Qatar, where he played all games as France finished the tournament as runner-ups.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ousmane Dembélé in the World Cups |url=https://www.thesoccerworldcups.com/players/ousmane_dembele.php |access-date=2023-07-26 |website=www.thesoccerworldcups.com |archive-date=25 September 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230925132931/https://www.thesoccerworldcups.com/players/ousmane_dembele.php |url-status=live }}</ref> Dembélé started the [[2022 FIFA World Cup final|final]] but conceded a penalty in the first half and was substituted in the 41st minute.<ref>{{cite web |last=Murray |first=Scott |date=18 December 2022 |title=2022 World Cup final: Argentina 3–3 France (aet, 4–2 on pens) – as it happened |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2022/dec/18/argentina-france-world-cup-2022-final-live?page=with:block-639f3b018f0834f3c057bd19&filterKeyEvents=false |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221218223853/https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2022/dec/18/argentina-france-world-cup-2022-final-live?page=with:block-639f3b018f0834f3c057bd19 |archive-date=18 December 2022 |access-date=18 December 2022 |website=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref>

On 18 November 2023, Dembélé scored a goal in a [[France v Gibraltar (UEFA Euro 2024 qualifying)|14–0]] win over [[Gibraltar national football team|Gibraltar]] during the [[UEFA Euro 2024 qualifying]], which was the largest win in the history of the France national team.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2023/11/19/sport/france-gibraltar-14-0-spt-intl/index.html |title=France beats Gibraltar a record 14–0 in Euro 2024 qualifier |publisher=CNN |date=19 November 2023 |access-date=10 April 2024 |archive-date=23 March 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240323125044/https://edition.cnn.com/2023/11/19/sport/france-gibraltar-14-0-spt-intl/index.html |url-status=live }}</ref> At the [[UEFA Euro 2024|final tournament]] in Germany, he was named [[Player of the match|man of the match]] in France's quarter-final victory against [[Portugal national football team|Portugal]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/euro2024/news/028f-1b4c52293b81-d35abf4d3953-1000--portugal-0-0-france-aet-3-5-pens-les-bleus-edge-through-on-/ |title=Portugal 0–0 France (aet, 3–5 pens): Les Bleus edge through on spot-kicks |website=[[UEFA]] |publisher=Union of European Football Associations |date=19 November 2023 |access-date=6 July 2024 |archive-date=6 July 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240706003056/https://www.uefa.com/euro2024/news/028f-1b4c52293b81-d35abf4d3953-1000--portugal-0-0-france-aet-3-5-pens-les-bleus-edge-through-on-/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

[[File:Ousmane Dembele France v Senegal 16 June 2026-263.jpg|thumb|upright|Dembélé with France at the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]]]]

On 14 May 2026, Dembélé was selected in the 26-man squad for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/48771039/france-2026-world-cup-squad-mbappe-camavinga-kolo-muani-dembele|title=France World Cup squad: Camavinga, Kolo Muani miss out|date=14 May 2026|access-date=17 June 2026|language=en}}</ref> In France's second group match on 22 June, he assisted [[Kylian Mbappé]]'s second goal and later scored his team's third in a 3–0 victory over [[Iraq national football team|Iraq]], which saw his side qualify for the knockout stages.<ref>{{cite web |title=Devastating Dembele seizes the spotlight |url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/articles/ousmane-dembele-france-iraq |publisher=www.fifa.com |access-date=24 June 2026 |date=22 June 2026 |archive-date=11 July 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260711040124/https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/articles/ousmane-dembele-france-iraq |url-status=live }}</ref> On 26 June, Dembélé scored a [[List of FIFA World Cup hat-tricks|hat-trick]] and was named Man of the Match in a 4–1 victory against [[Norway national football team|Norway]] in the final group stage match,<ref>{{Cite web |date=26 June 2026 |title=Ousmane Dembélé's first-half hat-trick sees France win group |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/49189907/ousmane-dembele-first-half-hat-trick-france |access-date=26 June 2026 |publisher=ESPN}}</ref> becoming the third French player to achieve this feat after [[Just Fontaine]] and [[Kylian Mbappé]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/6/26/dembele-scores-hat-trick-as-france-beat-norway-4-1-at-world-cup-2026 |title=Dembele scores hat-trick as France beat Norway 4-1 at World Cup 2026 |publisher=Al Jazeera |date=26 June 2026 |access-date=26 June 2026 |archive-date=26 June 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260626220405/https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/6/26/dembele-scores-hat-trick-as-france-beat-norway-4-1-at-world-cup-2026 |url-status=live }}</ref> In addition, he became the first player to score a first-half hat-trick since [[Oleg Salenko]] in 1994 and the second-fastest hat-trick from the start of the match after [[Erich Probst]] in 1954.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/articles/norway-france-match-highlights-report |title=Dembele hits terrific treble as France top group |publisher=FIFA |date=26 June 2026 |access-date=26 June 2026 |archive-date=20 July 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260720115249/https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/articles/norway-france-match-highlights-report |url-status=live }}</ref> In the round of 32 on 30 June, he set-up Mbappé's first goal in a 3–0 win over [[Sweden men's national football team|Sweden]].<ref>{{cite web |title=The French 'Fantastic Four' are in full swing |url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/articles/france-qualification-last-16-mbappe-dembele-olise-barcola |publisher=www.fifa.com |access-date=3 July 2026 |date=30 June 2026}}</ref> In the quarter-finals against [[Morocco national football team|Morocco]], he scored in a 2–0 victory, reaching five goals in a single World Cup edition and becoming only the third French player to achieve the feat after Just Fontaine and Kylian Mbappé.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/articles/france-morocco-match-report-highlights |title=Mbappe steers France into last four |publisher=FIFA |date=9 July 2026 |access-date=9 July 2026 |archive-date=19 July 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260719225806/https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/articles/france-morocco-match-report-highlights |url-status=live }}</ref> While Dembele scored in the third-place match against [[England national football team|England]], the French lost the match 4–6.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-07-18 |title= England take World Cup third place with 6-4 win against France|url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/england-take-world-cup-third-place-with-6-4-win-against-france-2026-07-18/|access-date=2026-07-18 |website=Reuters |language=en}}</ref>

==Player profile==
[[File:Ousmane Dembele France v Senegal 16 June 2026-378.jpg|thumb|upright|Dembélé playing for [[France national football team|France]] at the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]]|left]]

Dembélé is a [[Winger (association football)|winger]] who can play on either flank, due to his ability to use both feet, and to utilise his technical ability, speed, and [[agility]] in order to get past opponents or beat [[defender (association football)|defender]]s in one-on-one situations. Dembélé can also operate as a left or right-sided [[Midfielder#Attacking midfielder|attacking midfielder]] in a [[Formation (association football)#4–4–2|4–4–2]] or [[Formation (association football)#3–5–2|3–5–2]] formation. His clinical finishing and eye for goal also allow him to be deployed in a more offensive role as a [[Striker (association football)|striker]]. Dembélé also has great quality in terms of his shooting ability from distance.

Often described as one of the best players in the world,<ref name=":6" /><ref name=":7" /><ref name=":8" /> Dembélé has received praise from former team captain [[Andrés Iniesta]] for his game-changing qualities.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://en.as.com/en/2019/02/27/football/1551272729_055553.html |title=Arthur and Dembélé earn praise from Barcelona great Iniesta |newspaper=Diario AS |date=27 February 2019 |access-date=19 March 2019 |archive-date=24 November 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201124043406/https://en.as.com/en/2019/02/27/football/1551272729_055553.html |url-status=live }}</ref> He is well known for his [[Ambidexterity|ability to use either foot]];<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sport |date=2018-12-12 |title=Left or right footed? Ousmane Dembele's greatest skill and the stats |url=https://www.sport.es/en/news/barca/left-or-right-footed-ousmane-dembeles-greatest-skill-and-the-stats-7197272 |access-date=2022-12-14 |website=sport |language=en |archive-date=14 December 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221214234421/https://www.sport.es/en/news/barca/left-or-right-footed-ousmane-dembeles-greatest-skill-and-the-stats-7197272 |url-status=live }}</ref> a highly skilful player, his [[Dribbling#Association football|dribbling]] skills and ability to perform elaborate moves allow him to cut through from the left or right wing in order to score or create goalscoring opportunities for his teammates. The Frenchman is also an excellent [[Cross (association football)|crosser]] of the ball; moreover, his creativity is exceptional when in possession. Furthermore, his pace and intelligent runs make him a major offensive threat during [[counterattack]]s.

==Personal life==
===Religion===
Dembélé is a [[Muslims|Muslim]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=3 April 2022 |title=Así afecta el Ramadán al fútbol: el plan de los futbolistas musulmanes para jugar pese al ayuno |url=https://www.elespanol.com/deportes/futbol/20220403/afecta-ramadan-futbol-futbolistas-musulmanes-jugar-ayuno/661933915_0.html |access-date=16 April 2022 |website=El Español |language=es |archive-date=16 April 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220416224704/https://www.elespanol.com/deportes/futbol/20220403/afecta-ramadan-futbol-futbolistas-musulmanes-jugar-ayuno/661933915_0.html |url-status=live }}</ref> and observes [[Ramadan]], which requires him to [[Fasting during Ramadan|fast from dawn until sunset]] for roughly a month, including on training and match days.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2026-02-19|title=The Diet Lamine Yamal Will Follow During Ramadan|url=https://www.beinsports.com/en-us/soccer/la-liga/articles/the-diet-lamine-yamal-will-follow-during-ramadan-2026-02-19|access-date=2026-07-13|website=beIN SPORTS|language=en-us|archive-date=14 July 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260714185459/https://www.beinsports.com/en-us/soccer/la-liga/articles/the-diet-lamine-yamal-will-follow-during-ramadan-2026-02-19|url-status=live}}</ref>

musulmán|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/fc-barcelona/20211225/1001729462/boda-marroqui-dembele-rito-musulman.html|access-date=25 December 2021|website=Mundo September 2025 |archive-date=22 September 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250922235540/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/crmexzp11x3o |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Criticism===
In July 2021, video footage of Dembélé and teammate [[Antoine Griezmann]] circulated online, in which Dembélé makes racial comments towards Japanese technicians in his hotel room.<ref>{{Cite news|last=McTear|first=Euan|date=21 July 2019|title=Barcelona arrive in Japan and are ready to start pre-season|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/barcelona/2019/07/21/5d34303422601de1068b45b5.html|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|agency=[[EFE]]|access-date=3 July 2021|archive-date=9 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210709183424/https://www.marca.com/en/football/barcelona/2019/07/21/5d34303422601de1068b45b5.html|url-status=live}}</ref> As the technicians appear to be troubleshooting the room's television, Dembélé says to Griezmann in French: "All these ugly faces, just so you can play ''[[EFootball|PES]]'', aren't you ashamed? ... What the fuckin language?". As the video zooms in on the technicians' faces, Dembélé laughs and comments, "Are you technologically advanced in your country or not?".<ref>{{Cite news|last=White|first=Jonathan|date=3 July 2021|title=Euro 2020 star Ousmane Dembele in race storm for mocking Asian hotel workers in video with Antoine Griezmann|url=https://www.scmp.com/sport/football/article/3139698/euro-2020-star-ousmane-dembele-race-storm-mocking-asian-hotel|work=[[South China Morning Post]]|access-date=3 July 2021|archive-date=3 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210703225040/https://www.scmp.com/sport/football/article/3139698/euro-2020-star-ousmane-dembele-race-storm-mocking-asian-hotel|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Leaked video shows French football stars mocking Asian staff|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JzYtNz8o7S4|work=[[Turkish Radio and Television Corporation|TRT]]|language=en|access-date=10 November 2021|date=6 July 2021|archive-date=10 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211110011444/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JzYtNz8o7S4|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|last=Iaz|first=Chams|date=6 July 2021|title=Racisme anti-asiatique: les excuses insuffisantes de Ousmane Dembélé et Antoine Griezmann|language=fr|work=[[Le Temps]]|url=https://www.letemps.ch/societe/racisme-antiasiatique-excuses-insuffisantes-ousmane-dembele-antoine-griezmann|access-date=10 November 2021|issn=1423-3967|archive-date=10 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211110011428/https://www.letemps.ch/societe/racisme-antiasiatique-excuses-insuffisantes-ousmane-dembele-antoine-griezmann|url-status=live}}</ref>
